$comment: Reviewed thresholds for the admission gauntlet. These are DATA, not code:
changing one changes what the system will accept, so a change here is a
reviewed PR like any other. Values marked null are unset until Phase 1
records real baselines on real data — a guessed threshold that never
fires is worse than an absent one, because it reads as protection.

size.$comment_total: 160 MiB. Base scripture corpus is ~122 MiB; Layers A+B are budgeted ~30 MiB with headroom.
$comment_perTable: Per-table byte budgets, INCLUDING each table's indexes — an index ships with
its table and grows with it, so budgeting the table alone would miss two
thirds of what verse_terms actually costs.
Set 2026-07-30 from the first measured artifact (117.60 MiB total), with
headroom sized to intent rather than uniformly: verse_terms is the table that
grows when a commentator is admitted, so it gets room for roughly one more
whole-Bible author; the corpus tables are fixed by the translation and get
little. These are FIRST REAL VALUES and want Jesse's review — before today
these budgets named tables that did not exist and no gate read them.

FTS shadow tables are budgeted too: they are part of what ships, they grow with the corpus, and the gate reports any unbudgeted table over 1 MiB rather than passing it silently — which is how verses_fts_data was found.

$comment: p95 over the probe set, measured AFTER a warm-up pass, on whatever CI
runner GitHub provides. Deliberately loose relative to observed local
times (~5ms): a shared runner varies by several-fold, and a gate that
fails at random teaches people to ignore gates. What this catches is an
ALGORITHMIC regression - an accidental full scan, a dropped index - which
shows up as an order of magnitude, not a few milliseconds.
Target-hardware latency is a consumer's measurement, not this repo's.

collision.$comment: G4. Two concepts whose lexicons overlap beyond these thresholds are near-duplicates and must be merged or differentiated.

distinctiveness.$comment: G5. Terms below the PMI floor never enter a verse profile, so generic vocabulary cannot accumulate into evidence. The cap is PER VERSE since Layer B resolved to verse keys.

noise.$comment: G8. Measured against the previous artifact. Exceeding any of these fails the build and names the offending probes.
$comment_weak: Weak-reason share is gated as an INCREASE over baseline, not an absolute
ceiling. An absolute cap is meaningless while a query has no authoritative
signal available to it: a one-word thematic query like 'love' is 100% weak
in Phase 1 by construction, because concept anchors do not exist yet.
What we actually fear is the share CLIMBING as data accumulates - that is
precision erosion. So the delta is the gate and the absolute is recorded.

saturation.$comment: G9. A work that moves an already-covered pericope's profile less than minProfileDelta is recorded as saturated and skipped.
